name: TypeScript Agents: Vercel AI SDK and Mastra
question: How do I build agents in TypeScript, next to my web app?
summary: Many product teams work in TypeScript, and their agents live inside Next.js or Node services. The Vercel AI SDK is the common base: generateText and streamText run the tool loop with a step limit, tools are defined with Zod schemas, streaming UI hooks such as useChat render tokens and tool calls, and one line switches between model providers. Mastra builds on it with agents, workflows that can suspend for a human and resume later from storage, memory, RAG helpers and evals. LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Claude Agent SDK and Google ADK also have TypeScript versions; this tab is for teams who want a TypeScript-first stack.
useCases: Agents embedded in Next.js or Node products
Streaming chat and generative UI in the browser
Teams that want to switch model providers freely

steps.title: One package for the loop
steps.text: The ai package runs the model, the tools and the loop. Provider packages plug in underneath.

steps.title: Tools with Zod schemas
steps.text: Each tool has a description, a Zod input schema and an execute function. The schema becomes the JSON schema the model sees, and arguments are validated before execute runs.

steps.title: A bounded loop
steps.text: generateText keeps calling tools until the model answers or stopWhen ends it: here at 8 steps.

steps.title: Gate the risky tool
steps.text: This approval blocks the call. For approvals that take hours, a Mastra workflow suspends the run, stores its state and resumes when the reviewer answers.

steps.title: Switch providers in one line
steps.text: Swap anthropic() for openai() or google(); the tools and loop stay the same.

steps.title: Stream it to users
steps.text: In a Next.js route, streamText plus the useChat hook shows tokens and tool calls as they happen. About 24 lines for the same agent.

practice.scenario: Kosha Pay, a fictional UPI app, has a Next.js web team and no Python service. It builds the dispute agent with the Vercel AI SDK: two Zod-typed tools, generateText with an 8-step limit, and streamText with useChat so customers see progress live. Disputes needing a reviewer for hours move into a Mastra workflow that suspends, stores its state and resumes on approval. Switching model providers for a cost test took one line.

industries.use: Dispute and refund helpers inside the web app
Order-status agents in a Next.js storefront

practice.analogy: Adding a smart assistant to the shop counter you already run, instead of opening a second shop next door in a different language.

numericDrill.question: An agent route uses stopWhen: stepCountIs(8) and each step averages 1.2 s. What is the worst-case time in seconds before the step limit stops it?
numericDrill.answer: 8 × 1.2 = 9.6 s, close to common serverless limits; long cases belong in a workflow that can suspend.

interview.question: How would you build an agent inside a Next.js product?
interview.answer: Use the Vercel AI SDK: tools with Zod schemas, streamText with a step limit in a route handler, and useChat in the UI. Move approvals that take hours into a Mastra or LangGraph.js workflow that suspends and resumes.

interview.question: Why not block a request waiting for a human?
interview.answer: Serverless requests time out and hold resources; suspend the run, store state and resume when the reviewer answers.

mistakes.mistake: Long loops inside a short serverless request
mistakes.fix: Bound the steps, or run in a worker or workflow
